inventory.name: OpenET
inventory.claim: OpenET extended field-scale evapotranspiration estimates to all 48 contiguous states across its tools. USGS described OpenET as providing this service in September 2026.
inventory.limit: Coverage excludes Alaska and Hawaii. Estimates describe water transferred to the atmosphere, with model and observation limits. The cited update does not establish completeness of every current field or day.

inventory.name: Digital Earth Africa Water Observations from Space
inventory.claim: Digital Earth Africa released this continental surface-water classification service in September 2021. Its public catalogue records a Landsat 9 observation from 15 November 2026 with a derived WOfS scene created on 16 November. The associated classification file was publicly reachable on 17 November.
inventory.limit: The November check establishes production and access for one scene. Clouds, mixed land–water pixels and other conditions can obscure detections.

inventory.name: Advanced Land Imager on Earth Observing-1
inventory.claim: EO-1 ended operations after its extended mission. USGS retained access to the Advanced Land Imager's historical observations.
inventory.limit: January imaging wind-down and spacecraft shutdown were distinct milestones. The design contribution survives in operational Landsat hardware.

trace: Established design lineage: earth-observing-1-advanced-land-imager demonstrated a pushbroom imager in November 2000. Its focal-plane modules informed landsat-8-operational-land-imager, which acquired its first-light image in March 2013.

Established data link: OLI imagery supplies the Landsat 8 reflectance component of landsat-collection-2-global-level-2. Landsat 8 TIRS is a distinct instrument supplying the corresponding temperature component.

Established data branch: openet-field-scale-evapotranspiration makes field-scale water-use estimates. Its documented v2.0 SSEBop implementation uses Level-2 Landsat temperatures and accepts Landsat 8 scenes containing both reflectance and temperature bands.
Established data branch: digital-earth-africa-water-observations-from-space uses the Level-2 reflectance stream from landsat-collection-2-global-level-2 to classify the presence of surface water.

Established transfer: geoscience-australia-water-observations-from-space independently anchors the classifier lineage. The 2014 Australian product primarily used Landsat 5 and 7 imagery. Digital Earth Africa reused its decision tree on a new continental archive with African regional validation.
alternatives: A 2026 San Joaquin Valley comparison applied a separate USGS VIIRS-based SSEBop product alongside OpenET SSEBop. The common model family can be implemented with another sensor input. The comparison assesses one regional case and does not show that the VIIRS product offers OpenET's service or field detail. https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/water/articles/10.3389/frwa.2026.1879797/full

USGS separately offers a provisional on-demand Landsat evapotranspiration product with global scenes. It is a different service and output from OpenET's multi-model time-series estimates. https://www.usgs.gov/landsat-missions/news/landsat-product-supports-water-management-worldwide
frontier: Locate a versioned input manifest for the original October 2021 OpenET public release, by model, before attaching Collection 2 to that launch event.

Trace the Landsat 5/7 Australian archive and the Australian Geoscience Data Cube as separately bounded upstream achievements. Determine which component moved or was redeveloped for Digital Earth Africa.
Check how reliably annual WOfS summaries and scenes from other sensors or regions are updated. The November 2026 sample establishes one Landsat 9 processing result.
